messages.content: Ongoing: RoboRide drops price to $0.12 per mile. Wait time now 8 minutes. Coverage expanded to residential areas. Partnership wit
Local unemployment rising. Employment rate: 53%.
Consumer spending down. Spending index: 30 (baseline: 100).
You notice more robotaxis on the streets. About 7% of people seem to be using them regularly.
Auto sector revenue index: 79 (baseline: 100). Foot traffic and sales are somewhat down.

Business closing: Zoe Martinez — i have pitched two or three businesses over the past two ticks. this week i stop waiting for email replies. i call them directly or walk in. i am targeting: the diner (betty's if she is open to it, or the next closest), any small business near auto row that is still trying to maintain a social media presence and clearly does not have the bandwidth to do it well. my pitch is specific and economic: consumer spending is down 60% from baseline, foot traffic is soft, and local businesses that stay visible and humanly present on social media have a measurable edge over ones that go dark. i know how to do that. rate: $100 to $150 per month per client. goal this tick is to land at least one paying client. even $100 is real income at zero savings. if i close even one client before end of month, that is the first proof that the cert is not just a credential — my skills are already worth something to someone now.

Business closing: Stephanie Morris — follow up with amir patel today — by phone, not email — to close two things: the valuation fee for the tick 8 site visit, and a decision on what kind of ongoing engagement he wants. his inbox shows he is pursuing the ev charger financing and the chargepoint partnership proposal. he took the ev retrofit scenario from my four-scenario analysis and is executing on it — that is exactly what the analysis was designed to enable. my call acknowledges that directly: 'you are moving on the ev retrofit path. that is a real decision and the timeline you are working with — locking financing and getting the chargepoint proposal before committing — is exactly the right sequence.' then i ask the direct question: does he want me involved in the transaction side? if he pursues the ev retrofit and stays as owner-operator, he may eventually want to lease surplus space or sell the property in a converted state — that is a future listing. if the ev retrofit economics come back worse than expected from the chargepoint proposal, he may pivot to the sale path. either way, i want a clear engagement — either a consulting arrangement for the advisory work i have already done, or a listing agreement contingent on which path he chooses. the valuation fee for tick 8 was $1,500 — standard commercial property assessment fee for a two-hour site visit with written deliverables. i raise it directly, professionally, and i give him 30 days to pay it. i do not let the fee conversation linger indefinitely.

Business closing: Stephanie Morris — call betty kowalski after the task force session — late afternoon, not morning. i want to call her with something specific from the session: what the policy environment actually looks like right now, whether the licensing framework changes are going to be stabilizing or destabilizing for auto row, and whether the adaptive reuse permitting question came up. that is actionable intelligence that no one else will give her today. before the call, i know from word-of-mouth that she is attending kevin o'brien's office hours and exploring the roboride delivery partnership. i do not pretend i do not know this. i lead with it: 'i heard you went to kevin's office hours. smart move — knowing your financing options matters regardless of what you decide about the property.' that normalizes her deliberation without pressuring it. then i give her the task force read. then i ask the direct question i have been holding since tick 7: is she ready to walk the property with me and get the formal written valuation she can use with her landlord or a buyer? if yes, i bring the listing agreement. if not, i give her a specific deadline — not a pressure tactic, but an honest one: the spending index at 40 and employment at 67% mean the buyer pool is thinner every week. i will not tell her the window closes faster than it actually does. but i will tell her the truth, which is that the window is not getting wider.

Business closing: Stephanie Morris — make contact with patricia hawkins's office this week — or rick tanner directly if his relationship with stephanie can be established — about the dealership location that is being closed by end of q2. from the inbox intelligence: patricia is formally committing to close one sales floor location, and rick tanner is her analyst on the consolidation assessment. the service technicians are getting transfer offers; sales floor staff are being informed within a week. this means the property decision is coming within weeks, not months. i reach out with a specific, brief message that references my market brief from tick 1 and the nine ticks of auto row trajectory data i have compiled. the message is not a cold pitch — it is an introduction with a specific credential: 'i published an analysis of auto-adjacent commercial property on auto row in early tick 1 that specifically modeled dealership lot adaptive reuse scenarios. that analysis has tracked accurately through tick 9. i am the agent who has been working this corridor with current data for the full disruption period. if you are evaluating options for the location you are closing, i can provide a valuation and adaptive reuse demand mapping within 48 hours.' i do not oversell. i make one specific credentialed offer and give them a way to reach me.

Community action: Sarah Kim — reach out to zoe martinez this week — not to give advice, but to check in honestly. i know from word of mouth that she is investigating the roboride delivery partnership program and pivoting her gig strategy. i have been watching the same roboride expansion from a different angle: i am training to maintain the vehicles it deploys. we are in adjacent lanes of the same transition. i want to tell her that directly. not 'here is what you should do' — more like 'i see what you are doing and it makes sense from where you sit.' she has trust 0.56 in my network and i have formal power over her in the simulation topology, but i am not going to use that asymmetry. i am going to be a peer who is paying attention. if the conversation opens up naturally into the fleet maintenance angle — that the bike-based last-mile workers and the ev technicians are both part of the infrastructure roboride requires — i will share that frame. but i am not going in with an agenda.

Community action: Dorothy Chen — propose to lisa freeman at the community center that the transportation sessions i have been co-facilitating be expanded into a broader 'economic transition for older adults' workshop series — two sessions per month rather than one, covering not just transportation but also: how to evaluate whether to retrain at 60 or 70, how to talk to adult children about financial uncertainty without creating panic, and what community resources currently exist in millfield for people who are employed but precarious. the community stress level and protest count tell me that people do not just need transportation information. they need a space where the wider disruption can be named and worked through by people who are not in crisis themselves. i am not in crisis. i am a retired teacher with stable income and experience facilitating groups of adults. this is exactly the kind of thing i can offer and lisa's team cannot staff alone.
People around you are stressed: Betty Kowalski. The mood is tense.

You heard directly from Carlos Ruiz (Master Mechanic): Have a real conversation with Sarah Kim — not the version where I perform stability because I am the senior mechanic and she is the junior one. The version where I tell her what I actually know: that Rick called me, that the consolidation is real and moving faster than it was supposed to, that I am at month 5 of EVT Level 2 training and it is hard and worth it, and that the most important thing she can do right now is the same thing I am doing — build the credential that belongs to her and not to any specific floor. I will not predict whether her job survives the consolidation. I do not know. I will tell her what I do know: that being EV-certified changes her options whether she stays or goes. I will tell her that I am scared too, even if my timeline is longer. I will tell her that the fear is information, not prophecy.

You heard directly from Carlos Ruiz (Master Mechanic): Follow up with Miguel Hernandez on last tick's outreach. The word-of-mouth this tick says he is ready to have a direct conversation with me. I pick up the phone. I do not structure this as a mentorship conversation or a 'here is what you should do' conversation. I ask what he is actually facing: is the car wash seeing fewer vehicles? Is his employer talking about cuts? What does his financial runway look like? I am not a counselor and I do not pretend to have the answer for car wash workers in a robotaxi economy. But I am someone who has been sitting with this problem longer and who has made one concrete move — the certification — that I can describe honestly. If he asks, I tell him what the training cost, how long it takes, and whether I think it is working. I do not over-promise. I stay present.

You heard directly from Sarah Kim (Junior Mechanic): Begin concretely mapping the post-certification landscape: what organizations in the Millfield region and surroundings are likely to hire EV-certified technicians in the next 6-12 months? This is not a job application — it is research. I will ask Carlos for any names he has collected. I will look at what regional fleet operators exist — logistics, delivery, municipal vehicles, the RoboRide service infrastructure itself. I will identify whether there are any EV dealerships or service centers within commuting range. The cert completion date is approaching. I cannot arrive at completion without knowing what the next step is. My tick 6 reflection named this gap. I am closing it this tick.

You Immediately pick up maximum viable gig shifts this month — bike delivery via DoorDash and any last-mile delivery work that does not require a car. RoboRide's residential delivery expansion makes this viable as a last-mile layer: the robotaxi brings the package close, I deliver the final block. Research the RoboRide delivery partner registration process this week — if it pays better than DoorDash bike routes, shift hours toward it. Target: 15 to 20 hours of gig work per week across evenings and weekends, carefully scheduled so it does not conflict with Tuesday/Thursday evening classes and Saturday morning class. This is not a career pivot. This is survival. The goal is to generate $400 to $600 this month — enough to stop the savings bleed while I stay enrolled in the cert program. At $1,180 in savings and $1,200/month in essentials, I have less than one month of runway. This is the constraint that overrides everything except keeping my cert streak alive.. Savings dropped by $1,180.
